senses.label: Stoic therapy of the passions
senses.summary: Distress comes from false judgements about what is good or bad; correcting the judgement removes the passion.
markers: it is not things that disturb us but our judgements about them
a passion is cured by correcting a false belief
hazards: Modern cognitive therapy openly borrowed this from Epictetus, so the model may blur the two. The old sense is Marcus's own; the clinical method is not.

sources.citation: Chrysippus, On Passions, book IV 'Therapeutikon' (lost; reported by Galen)
sources.note: The Stoic therapy of the passions.
Latin account of the Stoic cure of distress.
'It is not things that disturb people, but their judgements about things.'

senses.label: Psychoanalysis
senses.summary: Symptoms come from unconscious conflicts, relieved by talking freely to an analyst.
markers: talking to an analyst over many sessions relieves them

sources.citation: Breuer and Freud, Studies on Hysteria (1895)

senses.label: Cognitive and behavioural therapy
senses.summary: A structured clinical method in which a therapist helps a patient identify and test distorted thoughts.
markers: thoughts are tested like hypotheses in structured sessions
a therapist treats anxiety as a clinical condition
'therapy' means a course of sessions with a trained professional

sources.citation: Albert Ellis, rational therapy, from 1955; A. T. Beck, cognitive therapy, 1960s
sources.note: Ellis cites Epictetus as a source.
